name: memory_remember
description: Stores one memory in the long-term memory of this workspace: a stable fact, a decision with its reason, a preference, or context about a person or project that the user stated or confirmed. Use it when the user asks you to remember something, or states such a fact plainly; never store guesses, one-off chatter or secrets (it refuses text that looks like a key, token or password). Storing the same text again returns the existing id instead of a copy. It does not search (that is memory_search) or hide memories (that is memory_archive). Returns the id; tell the user in one line what was stored.

text.description: The memory itself, one or two plain sentences (e.g. Clara Client wants invoices on the 1st of each month).

kind.description: What it is: fact, decision, preference, person, project or note (e.g. preference).

tags.description: Comma-separated tags, at most 8, such as a project key or a name (e.g. clara-client,proj-123).

source.description: Where it came from, in a few words (e.g. user in chat, email from someone@example.com).

examples.text: Clara Client wants invoices on the 1st of each month.
PROJ-123 uses PostgreSQL because the team already runs it.
